title: Development of a lead foil crown delineation technique for implant rehabilitations to generate patient specific finite element model of occlusal loading points
author: Sundar S, Shetty, et al.

steps.title: Obtain patient consent
steps.instruction: Secure written informed consent from the patient before any clinical or imaging procedures are performed.

steps.title: Acquire initial CBCT scan
steps.instruction: Perform a cone‑beam CT (CBCT) of the target area (single missing tooth or edentulous jaw) and export DICOM files with a resolution of 0.29 mm × 0.29 mm and a slice thickness of 0.6 mm to assess alveolar and basal bone volume.

steps.title: Fabricate PMMA prosthetic tooth
steps.instruction: Under strict aseptic precautions, fabricate the patient‑specific prosthetic tooth or complete denture in polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA), positioning the tooth/teeth in occlusion with the opposing arch and setting the denture in centric relation (customised rest position of upper and lower jaws).

steps.title: Contour lead foil over crown
steps.instruction: Disinfect the fabricated prosthetic tooth/denture, then contour a 0.5 mm‑thick malleable lead foil over each crown using a wax carver, surgical knife No. 11, B.P. handle No. 3 and non‑cyanoacrylate glue; ensure the foil adapts without overlap, does not extend onto gums or adjacent teeth, and is positioned correctly in occlusion before inserting the foil‑contoured denture onto the edentulous jaws.

steps.title: Acquire CBCT with lead foil
steps.instruction: Repeat the CBCT scan (same resolution: 0.29 mm × 0.29 mm, slice thickness 0.6 mm) with the lead‑foil‑contoured prosthesis in place to obtain DICOM images showing radio‑opaque delineation of the occlusal surfaces (lead foil appears radiopaque, PMMA and denture flanges remain radiolucent).

steps.title: Generate 3D assembly
steps.instruction: Import the DICOM data into MIMICS (Materialise’s Interactive Medical Image Control System), segment and render the alveolar bone, lead‑foil crown, and surrounding structures; create virtual implants of customized dimensions positioned according to bone‑volume assessment, and model a 2 mm cylindrical titanium bar connecting all implants to the virtual occlusal surface, replicating the laboratory prosthetic design.

steps.title: Perform finite element analysis
steps.instruction: Assign material properties from Table 1 (e.g., titanium E = 110 GPa, ν = 0.35; cancellous bone E = 1.37 GPa, ν = 0.3; etc.) to the segmented 3D model, mesh it anisotropically, and analyse it in Abaqus/CAE® v6.13‑1; vary load application points (central fossa, buccal cusp, lingual cusp) and load magnitudes, compute von Mises stress distribution, and determine the optimal implant dimensions, position and angulation.

steps.title: Place implants surgically
steps.instruction: Using 3D‑printed surgical guides based on the FE‑derived plan, place the dental implants into the alveolar bone at the determined positions and angulations; verify implant placement radiographically during the postoperative period.
